title: Electrode-tunable nonlocal Rashba-Edelstein effect and layer-selective chirality switch in WSe$_2$-intercalated bilayer graphene
authors: Marko Milivojević, Juraj Mnich, Martin Gmitra
abstract: We show that intercalating a WSe$_2$ monolayer into bilayer graphene creates a synthetic bilayer graphene at the Fermi level, in which WSe$_2$-mediated wavefunction overlap hybridizes the two graphene layers, giving rise to states delocalized across both layers. Because the interlayer coupling is comparable in energy to the proximity-induced spin-orbit interaction, the resulting spintronic behavior goes beyond what is typically accessible in conventional single-interface proximity systems. A simple four-electrode device, with source and drain electrodes on both the top and bottom graphene layers, gives access to distinct regimes depending on which electrodes are activated. The most prominent feature is a nonlocal Rashba-Edelstein effect, activated via cross-layer source and drain electrodes, in which a charge current injected into one graphene layer generates a spin accumulation in the spatially separated opposite layer. This effect is robust to the twist angle modulation between graphene and WSe$_2$ and to the applied electric field, suggesting that a moderate degree of structural asymmetry along the vertical direction does not destroy it. In addition, activating the source and drain electrodes on either the top or bottom graphene layer reveals local Rashba-Edelstein signals of opposite sign in the two layers, thereby realizing a layer-selective chirality switch. This is a consequence of the hidden Rashba effect, which is present even when a net Rashba splitting is forbidden. Our results suggest new physical regimes and device architectures that could be useful for spintronic applications.
summary: This work theoretically explores charge-spin conversion in WSe2-intercalated bilayer graphene, creating a synthetic platform where interlayer coupling is crucial. The authors predict the observation of nonlocal Rashba-Edelstein effects and layer-selective spin signals by tuning external fields or twist angles. This suggests new device architectures for spintronics that leverage engineered quantum couplings.
main_problem: The study investigates novel spintronic phenomena, specifically the nonlocal Rashba-Edelstein effect and layer-selective chirality switching, in a synthetic bilayer graphene system.
main_result: The authors demonstrate that interlayer hybridization allows for distinct spin transport signatures, including nonlocal charge-to-spin conversion and opposite-sign local signals, which are robust to structural variations.
method: Theoretical calculations using the Kubo formula within the Smrčka-Streda formulation were employed to compute charge-spin conversion coefficients ($\alpha_{	ext{REE}}$ and $\alpha_{	ext{UREE}}$).
model_or_system: The system is a WSe2-intercalated bilayer graphene, which forms a synthetic bilayer structure where interlayer coupling competes with proximity-induced spin-orbit interaction. The analysis uses an effective Hamiltonian incorporating valley-dependent interlayer interactions.
key_observables: Nonlocal Rashba-Edelstein effect coefficients ($\alpha_{S_t-D_b}^{	ext{REE}}$), layer-selective local signals, and the unconventional Rashba coefficient ($\alpha_{	ext{UREE}}$).
important_parameters: Twist angle ($	heta$), perpendicular electric field ($E$), doping/chemical potential ($\mu$), and the relative strength of interlayer coupling versus SOC.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes weak disorder scattering, and that the hybridization places the system beyond the perturbative regime of standard proximity heterostructures.
figures_summary: Figures detail the dependence of $\alpha_{	ext{REE}}$ and $\alpha_{	ext{UREE}}$ on doping for various twist angles and electric fields, showing component contributions (e.g., St-Dt, Sb-Db) that confirm distinct physical mechanisms at play.
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes the system's symmetries ($\sigma_h$) to predict zero global effects, then explores how breaking these symmetries via external fields ($E$) or twist angles ($	heta$) reveals hidden and nonlocal spin transport phenomena using detailed Kubo calculations.
why_interesting: While focused on condensed matter spintronics, the concept of emergent, tunable quantum couplings (interlayer hybridization) leading to non-trivial transport coefficients is relevant for understanding engineered quantum materials interfaces.

figures.caption: Figure 1. Schematics of the WSe2-intercalated bilayer graphene device. The WSe2 monolayer mediates interlayer overlap between the top and bottom graphene layers, form- ing a synthetic bilayer graphene at the Fermi level. The global horizontal mirror plane symmetry σh of the heterostructure forbids the presence of the apparent Rashba effects and leads to mutual compensation of local Rashba contributions from the top and bottom graphene/WSe2 interface. Figure 2. Calculated electronic structure of the zero twist angle graphene/WSe2/graphene heterostructure in the vicin- ity of the graphene K point. The calculation of the atomic wave projection suggests that the bands around the K point are constructed by approximately equal contributions of the top and bottom layers. Formed delocalized molecular-like or- bitals support the theory of the creation of a synthetic bilayer graphene, mediated by the WSe2 monolayer.

Figure 3. Calculated charge-spin conversion coefficients αREE as a function of doping for different experimental configura- tions sketched in FIG. 1: source/drain electrodes are config- ured on top (St/Dt) and bottom (Sb/Db) graphene layers. These are selectively activated as: situation 1 (all electrodes on: St, Sb, Dt, Db, labeled as Total); situation 2 (lateral: St-Dt and Sb-Db); and situation 3 (crossed: St-Db and Sb- Dt). Top (a) and bottom (b) panels correspond to different values of the quasiparticle lifetime, whose values are given on the graphs. The sharp peaks at EF −µ ≈−1.25 meV and EF −µ ≈+1.32 meV originate from band crossings away from the K point.

Spintronics.note: This work provides a theoretical calculation of charge-to-spin conversion (nonlocal Rashba-Edelstein effect) in an engineered spintronic heterostructure (WSe2-intercalated bilayer graphene), directly fitting the theme of spin transport in novel materials.
